🌈 SUPER SIMPLE TASTE-SAFE KINETIC SAND 🌈 If you’re looking for kid safe kinetic sand - this is it! It might not have the silicone binder that store bought has which gives a stretchy effect, but it’s made with 5 simple ingredients, that still gives it the ability to be squished and moulded while holding its shape and it crumbles like sand. It’s fun, cheap, and so easy to whip up… plus your little ones will love it! INGREDIENTS: 1 cup baking soda 1/2 cup sugar 3/4 cup cornflour  1 Tbsp cream of tartar 1/4 cup of water 1 tsp food colouring (optional) HOW TO: 1. Add the baking soda, sugar, cornflour, and cream of tartar to a large bowl, and stir  everything together. 2. In a small cup, mix your food colouring & water (if you’re using food colouring). 3. Add 2 Tbsp of the water into the dry mix and whisk together. If its still too powdery and doesn’t clump in your hands, add 1 Tbsp more of the water, and stir again. Repeat up to the full 1/4 cup of water, squishing with your hands to mix it in and get the right texture (note if you get heavy handed with the water, counterbalance it by adding equal parts cornflour & sugar, 1 Tbsp of each at a time) 4. Enjoy! NOTES: 🫙 Store in an airtight container in the fridge for 4–6 weeks. If it dries out a little, add 1–2 tsp of water and mix it through with your hands. 🌈  you can make the colour brighter by adding a few extra drops into the water at the beginning. 👶 whilst this recipe is taste-safe, make sure to supervise little ones closely as it’s not for eating by the handful.  . . . . . #kineticsand #toddler #kidsactivities #sensoryplay #playtolearn

Huge congrats to disability arts ensemble #KineticLight for making their #LincolnCenter debut last weekend with their show, Under Momentum! Using ramps designed by Sara Hendren, dancers Alice Sheppard and Laurel Lawson explored momentum, speed, balance, and the pull of gravity in their performance. Check out these highlights from their performance! Video Description: Clips of dancers Alice Sheppard, a multiracial Black woman with curly hair, and Laurel Lawson, a white dancer with short blue hair; they both wear metallic leggings and sleeveless tops. As they dance the stage lighting shifts from deep purple to bright sunset orange to vibrant green. Alice and Laurel dance in their wheelchairs, spinning around each other. They separate and Laurel goes up and down a ramp. They come back together and spin again. The scene shifts: Alice and Laurel are balancing back to back on a ramp, each with their inside hand held out. They turn around and head up the ramp.  The scene shifts: Laurel holds Alice (legs on her lap, torso draped over Laurel's shoulder) and spins around. Laurel puts Alice down and they wheel away in opposite directions. The scene shifts: ASL Interpreter Daniel Israilov of SignNexus, a tall man wearing glasses, performs the music in ASL. Alice and Laurel are behind him going up and down two ramps. The scene shifts: Alice climbs over Laurel, lands on her forearms, and then crawls, pulling Laurel behind her. Alice somersaults as Laurel tips herself forward, coming to an upright position. A final scene shift: the dancers are each on ramps on opposite sides of the stage gently rocking back and forth as the lights go dark. Audio: An excerpt of "you" by Jonathan Paulsen with moody sounds of string instruments and claps/clicks dispersed throughout.
